problem: It says "one mutual term is negative" when the series current enters one dot and leaves the other. With one series current the sign of both mutual terms flips: for coil 1, i₂ enters an undotted terminal, so v₁ = L₁di/dt − M di/dt; for coil 2, i₂ also enters an undotted terminal, so v₂ = −M di/dt + L₂di/dt. A student who carries "one negative" into the two-equation form will get the wrong sign.
fix: Write: "If i enters one dot and leaves the other dot, both mutual terms become negative. The total voltage is v = (L₁ + L₂ − 2M) di/dt, called series opposing."

problem: "Some syllabi call this dot conversion; the standard name is the dot convention." The sentence is attached to the sign flip, but dot conversion (or dot shifting) normally means moving a dot to the other terminal and adjusting the sign. As written, the two ideas get mixed and a student may think flipping the sign and moving a dot are the same operation.
fix: Drop the naming sentence, or separate it: "The sign rule above defines the dot convention. Moving a dot to the other terminal of a coil reverses the sign of that coil's mutual term; some books call that dot conversion."

problem: v₁ and v₂ are called "the voltages at the dotted terminals", but a terminal voltage needs a reference. The KVL equations only hold when each voltage is measured from the dotted terminal to the undotted terminal of the same coil.
fix: "v₁ and v₂ are the voltages of coils 1 and 2 measured from the dotted terminal to the undotted terminal; i₁ and i₂ enter those dotted terminals."

problem: "At k = 1 with equal coils, the aiding formula is read as a limit and stays finite" stops short of the value. For L₁ = L₂ = L and M = kL, the aiding fraction is L²(1 − k²)/[2L(1 − k)], which tends to L(1 + k)/2 and gives L at k = 1.
fix: Add the value: "At k = 1 with equal coils the aiding formula is 0/0; taking the limit gives L_eq → L(1 + k)/2 = L."

problem: The sentence "If a current enters an undotted terminal, the sign of its M term becomes negative" repeats the prose sentence just above the box, so the same point is made twice in two lines.
fix: Keep the rule once, either in the prose or in the box, not both.
